areas.finding: No governed connectors reach the systems the business runs on; the TMS, ledger and customs platform are all unreachable by the assistant, and requests to connect things arrive weekly with no framework to receive them.
areas.action: Decide the first connection deliberately (the TMS, read-only, scoped) and let it set the pattern.

areas.finding: The file layer is chosen and syncing but was migrated without reorganisation; findability is the sponsor's most-heard complaint, and the answer to the customers' most-asked question lives in a spreadsheet that is updated late.
areas.action: Structure before search: department-led reorganisation with IT stating what AI-readable structure means.

areas.finding: The interim usage note bans customer commercial data, personal data and carrier rates from the assistant, which is a real considered position; no fuller mapping from data classes to AI use exists in writing.
areas.action: Map the existing classifications to AI use before a client questionnaire asks.

areas.finding: No home sits over the operational and financial truths; the weekly pack and 6 hours of reconciliation are the visible cost, and the largest single unlock in the discovery waits here.
areas.action: Get to an owned, dated decision on a minimum useful internal data capability.

areas.finding: The assistant is licensed deliberately at about 60 seats; embedded AI arrives by vendor update with no decision and no list of surfaces exists.
areas.action: Enumerate where AI runs; an hour with a spreadsheet the policy can then govern.

areas.finding: Nothing unattended runs anywhere except one analyst's laptop; the automation the official quoting process depends on stops when he is away.
areas.action: Pick the rates pull as the first managed-runtime candidate and settle identity in the same move.

areas.finding: The one business-critical automation authenticates as its author; nothing defines how an automation should run as the business.
areas.action: Decide what the first hosted automation runs as before it is rebuilt.

areas.finding: TMS permissions are coarse (everyone operational sees everything), named by IT as the blocker to any assistant connection, and no record of what anything can reach exists.
areas.action: Make read-only and per-connection scoping the default before the first connector, while the estate is one item long.

areas.finding: An interim note covers the assistant with a real review-before-reliance clause; it covers nothing embedded, names no owner, and was written to be revisited when the picture settles, which it has.
areas.action: Grow the note into a policy with an owner and embedded-AI coverage now, not at an annual review.

areas.finding: Approval genuinely happens and is sane, but it is one person's email judgement with no record, and AI-related requests now arrive weekly.
areas.action: Add the record and split fast items from slow ones before volume makes it a queue.

areas.finding: Nothing routes an AI incident anywhere; the wrong cut-off reached a customer and no process noticed, the customer did.
areas.action: Route AI incidents into whatever incident handling exists, and note the trigger waits on telemetry.

areas.finding: The note requires competent review and nothing implements it: the FAQ assistant died on one unverifiable answer, the customs clerk and the sales lead both name verification as their condition for trust.
areas.action: Build one verification harness and prove it on the cut-off answers first.

areas.finding: The admin console, reviewed together, shows spend for this month and last and nothing else: no per-user or per-team usage, no activity.
areas.action: Collect what the current plan exposes before considering any tier change.

areas.finding: No per-event trail exists for the assistant, and nobody has established what the other surfaces log; the approval trail is an email thread.
areas.action: Establish what each surface logs as part of the estate inventory.

areas.finding: Nothing beyond the invoice says what assistant use achieves; the sponsor states the question plainly and nobody can answer it.
areas.action: Baseline three measures now, starting with cycle time on the quote-to-booking stream.

areas.finding: Spend is noticed and rising and cannot be attributed to a team or an outcome; at about 60 seats it could be derived by hand once.
areas.action: Derive it by hand this quarter; automation waits on usage visibility.

areas.finding: Real bottom-up use exists in every function visited: a working booking-entry prototype, assistant-built finance views, drafted quote emails; the ceiling is individual, one tool per person with outputs moved by hand.
areas.action: Teach the step beyond individual use in protected time, on the builders' own examples.

areas.finding: Nothing is shared or taught; a builder stopped partly because he was unsure he was allowed, which is what an absence of shared practice looks like from below.
areas.action: One protected half-day, built around the prototypes that already exist.

areas.finding: No route exists from a working build to shared use; the booking prototype and the abandoned FAQ assistant both stranded on exactly this.
areas.action: Stand up the review-and-publish route with the booking prototype as its first case.

areas.finding: Nobody owns making AI work; the default owner is a two-person IT team already living in the backlog, observed directly across the session, and no forum exists where the decisions in this report would be taken.
areas.action: Name one accountable owner with protected time, and protect IT's learning time explicitly.
